questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Bristol was my 3rd choice, but I really wanted to go to the UK. I knew nothing about Bristol and the University before I went, but ended up really loving it!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a long and at times difficult and confusing progress, to apply for study abroad, but the experience once I was there made it all worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Bristol university was very helpful and sent out a lot of very informative emails that helped me know what to do when I arrived and where to go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The staff and my uni accommodation were very helpful and gave me a very nice welcome.
The university was also very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I do wish, however, that the university had helped me with the social events of the more local students a little more. Freshers week is a big thing for all the new students, the 1. years, and I didn't really know what was going on socially for a while.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of options on campus. Both Student 'halls' and other dorms. I lived in a very large student accommodation where we lived in flats in 5-6 people 'groups'.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The cooking facilities at my accommodation were good. We (6 people) shared a big kitchen and it worked well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
In a lot of the campus housing in Bristol you will have to buy all of your own kitchen supplies and a lot of stuff for your room as well. So for me it kind of felt like I was buying a whole new kitchen and went to IKEA in Bristol to get everything I needed. I probably spent about 110 pounds in total for kitchen and room supplies.
I know that some people will go out and buy supplies together with their flat/roomates, which I think makes a bit more sense money wise, but my flatmates had bought all their own stuff, so I did the same.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I found the course registration quite tedious and confusing, because I was sent/shown the wrong list. So I chose some courses and was then told I couldn't choose them, I then chose some others and were also told there were problems with them. Some of the courses I knew I wanted to do on my time abroad, such as "Creative Writing" was shown in their catalogue, but weren't available for international students.

In the end, I ended up asking for a phone call from their registration office, because it was confusing to keep sending emails back and forth. The phone call was very helpful and we quickly figured out my courses. The staff at UoB are all very nice and helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Their staff are all very helpful.
If you wanted to ask about a course or change one you could go talk to some of the staff and it was really nice just to sit down and have a talk about it. I never felt like I was all alone in figuring these things out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all the courses I had originally wanted, but I ended up being quite happy with my courses. I had one course where I went to the first seminar and quickly knew I didn't want to take that course. In the first two weeks it is possible to change courses and that process was luckily both very quick and easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask! it is okay to send a lot of emails and even to ask for phone calls to talk about thing. There are no dumb questions and they are happy to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my courses and thought my teachers were great!!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 2nd year courses and one 3rd year course and really liked all of them. I originally had one 1st year course and quickly realized it was too 'beginner' level for me and I also didn't like the subject, so I ended up changing it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures and seminars were all shorter than I am used to at UCPH, but I really liked them and thought they were very engaging and motivating

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENGL20139 Early Modern Women Writers
ENGL29008 Revenge Tragedy
ENGL30115 Novel Territories: Eighteenth-century Prose Fiction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like literature and specifically 'women writers' I can highly recommend the two courses 'ENGL20139 Early Modern Women Writers' and 'ENGL30115 Novel Territories: Eighteenth-century Prose Fiction'.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Just to clarify my spending.
I saved 30,000.00 DKK up for my trip, and spent all of it. I did all the things I wanted and went on some trips, I went to Oxford, Bath, other one day trips and also longer ones: a weekend in Leeds, 4 days in London and a week in Edinburgh. 
So I wouldn't say I spent a lot of money per. month just for 'living', but I bought stuff, went out to restaurants and went on trips, and that's probably what I spent the most money on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food in Bristol is cheaper, in the supermarkets, than in Copenhagen, so that was nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bristol University had a lot of social societies. Basically one for every interest you could imagine: sports, creative and academic. I really enjoyed these and the social aspects of them!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some societies at the university! They are a lot of fun and a great way to make friends!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips!! There are so many great and beautiful places to see near Bristol and the university Student Union also plans a lot of great trips you can buy and go on. Explore!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Bristol/the UK are definitely different from Copenhagen and Denmark in some ways, but not very different. I found it pretty easy to adjust and even found that the people in Bristol are a lot kinder and friendlier to strangers than we are in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and vulnerable! I made a lot of nice friends, some from my courses and some from the societies. I found that it's really okay to just say "Hi, I'm not from here and I would really like to make some new friends!", a lot of the time I was met with people introducing me to their friend groups and inviting me to different things which made me feel very welcome.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are very open, friendly and kind. I miss that now that I'm home! Being called 'love' and 'darling' by people is just so heartwarming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't know anything about Bristol beforehand and honestly didn't have that high expectations but I loved it! The city has so much life, culture, charm and warmth and I felt really at home. Bristol University also have some beautiful buildings that I really loved.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Something new that happened in my semester was hand written exams. This was a new thing for everyone, but something they did to avoid people using AI in their essays. So it was a 2 hour exam set in a big hall were we wrote out essays with pen on paper.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The feeling of freedom that you only feel while living on your own in a new country! And the personal growth!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trusting yourself and the timing. You might have a lot of expectations as to what you semester abroad 'should' look like, but whatever happens and whatever you do is great and 'enough'.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Why was I not informed that there were travel reports like this that I could read before my semester abroad??

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
